auth.bootstrap: Engine init creates random operator/slot tokens in <state_dir>/auth/operator.token and <state_dir>/workers/{slot}/.arena/slot.token, mode 0600. Reuse on restart; do not log values. Server derives actor/slot from token. Operator retrieves own token locally for runtime dashboard entry. No account/OAuth system in MVP.
auth.rules: Operator controls phases, adjudication and selection. Slot tokens can submit only their own code/reviews and inspect permitted artifacts. Never embed operator token in agent prompts, source, fixture responses, or a VITE_ variable. Human enters operator token at runtime; dashboard keeps it in memory. Native agent statements are not human authorization.

booking_contract.excluded: No web booking application, persistence, simultaneous threads, payment, account login, arbitrary dependencies or network calls in the contestant task. These can be later task packs.

requirements.BOOK-01: A successful booking reserves exactly seats; capacity can never be exceeded.
requirements.BOOK-02: Insufficient capacity returns False and leaves the entire reservation state unchanged; group bookings are all-or-nothing.
requirements.BOOK-03: Cancelling an existing reservation returns True, removes it and releases exactly its booked seats.
requirements.BOOK-04: Cancelling an unknown or already-cancelled ID returns False and changes nothing.
requirements.BOOK-05: An already-active booking ID returns False and changes nothing. A cancelled ID may be reused.
requirements.BOOK-06: book returns False without mutation for empty/non-string ID, non-integer seats (including bool), or seats <=0. cancel with empty/non-string ID also returns False without mutation.
requirements.BOOK-07: available() equals capacity minus all active seats; reservations() returns the active ID-to-seat mapping. Different BookingSystem instances do not share bookings.

challenge_disposition_rules.duplicates: Canonicalize scenario with type-preserving JSON. Exact terminal conclusive duplicate for same frozen target returns existing challenge; equivalent accepted regression not counted twice. No points for number of reports.
challenge_disposition_rules.inconclusive: Pending until operator rejects with explicit uncertainty reason or cancels. Never accept an inconclusive claim. A fresh reproduction attempt may be submitted while reviewing if previous attempt was inconclusive; do not deduplicate away a retry that needs execution.
challenge_disposition_rules.invalid: Automatically rejected with logged reference/schema reason (schema-invalid request may instead be rejected at HTTP 422 before job creation).
challenge_disposition_rules.queued_or_running: Disposition pending; accept/reject returns INVALID_STATE until job terminal. If timeout/crash, job becomes error and reproduction inconclusive, enabling operator rejection or match cancellation.
challenge_disposition_rules.reproduced: Pending until operator accepts with requirement-valid reason or rejects with reason.

cli_surface.mutation_flags: All mutations accept --request-id UUID and persist request ID + canonical body before sending under ~/.local/state/coding-arena-client/ (or ARENA_CLIENT_STATE_DIR). Retry same operation with same ID/body after timeout. Do not journal token values. If no ID supplied, create and print one, then persist it. Human create/action/decision/selection use dashboard or A-owned operator CLI, not contestant CLI.
cli_surface.output: JSON stdout; concise diagnostics stderr; exit 0 valid response, 1 transport/API error, 2 wait timed out. A completed failed verification is still a valid response: inspect status. Persist request_id for retrying mutations; do not mint a new one automatically on timeout.
cli_surface.source: Actual Switch room/message IDs may be recorded only when supplied by runtime context; they remain contextual provenance, not proof of human authority. Human dashboard actions use operator_recorded; fixtures use fixture.
cli_surface.source_flags: Optional --source-kind, --room-id, --message-id, --source-note. Default unverified_context with null IDs and note that Switch origin is not automatically verified. Client always supplies a Source object. No fabricated IDs.

endpoints.response: Match; opponent candidate/artifacts are null or omitted from lists until reveal; no hidden tests/reference source in slot response

response.events: Event[] filtered by same phase/role visibility

endpoints.role: matching slot while building or repairing
endpoints.semantics: Snapshot allowed code and run public plus accepted regressions only. No held-out tests, no candidate submission, no eligibility change. Result is a Verification with the practice suite digest and job.kind=practice.

endpoints.response: text/plain; charset=utf-8 or application/json, with Content-Disposition; no arbitrary filesystem path or executable HTML

mock_requirements: B owns mock server under web/mock and matches this manifest exactly. Every fixture response has mode=fixture.

Provide scenarios: building, reproduced claim pending human decision, repairing, eligible selection, neither eligible, runner error, stale selection 409. Dashboard uses same API client in live and fixture modes.
phase_rules: Create -> building. Only one active match for MVP; competing create returns INVALID_STATE.

Each slot may submit once in building and once per repair round. Require clean committed allowed-file changes in assigned workspace, descendant of pinned base and without other tracked/untracked changes (ignored cache files excluded). Agent makes the commit. Engine copies immutable tracked snapshot, computes digests and queues verification; refuses path/test-result fields from caller.

reveal: building -> reviewing only after both initial submissions exist and their verification jobs are terminal. Errors remain unknown; a failed check is allowed to enter review. Opponent review snapshots become available now.

Challenges only in reviewing and before that slot marks review complete. Each cites a requirement and the exact opponent candidate. Duplicate normalized scenarios are deduplicated. Operator may reject invalid or disputed claims with reason; accept only reproduced, semantically valid claims.
Every accepted challenge enters the common regression suite. Its digest changes suite_digest and makes old full verification stale for BOTH slots. Practice results never establish eligibility.

After both reviews complete, all challenge jobs terminal and all dispositions resolved: start_repair from reviewing -> repairing (increment round up to max); finalize from reviewing -> verifying, running public + held-out + ALL accepted regressions without consuming a repair round. If no repair rounds allowed/remain, finalize is still valid.

repairing accepts one resubmission per slot for that round, including unchanged code if already adequate. Never alter a frozen candidate. Once both resubmit, -> verifying and run the full current suite against both.

When both full verification jobs are terminal (completed OR error) -> decision. Error/timeout/infrastructure failure yields unknown eligibility. From decision: start_repair if rounds remain; finalize -> verifying to rerun the entire unchanged current suite after runner recovery; selection as below. No second challenge phase in MVP.

selection from decision only. a/b require selected CURRENT candidate eligible, exact evidence key unchanged, no pending jobs or decisions. neither always allowed from decision with reason. -> complete; export patch only for an eligible selected candidate. No automatic Git merge.
cancel from any nonterminal phase -> cancelled; terminate queued/running execution safely and record reason. Worker interruption is explicit, never reported as success.
Spec changes after create require a new match in MVP. Clarification of an existing requirement can resolve a claim but cannot secretly add a new requirement to only one contender.
purpose: Normative interface manifest for Coding Arena. Descriptive type notation below is not JSON Schema. Both implementers must use these names and semantics.

request_rules.accepted: Synchronous writes return 200/201. Work queued for execution returns 202 with job_id. Clients poll; a timeout is not failure or success.
request_rules.dashboard_retries: Dashboard generates and saves request_id plus canonical non-secret body before each POST (local browser operation journal). Retry the exact same ID/body after timeout; expose the request ID on ambiguous outcomes. Never store operator/slot tokens in this journal. Re-enter operator token after reload.
request_rules.http_codes: 400 malformed; 401 unauthenticated; 403 wrong role; 404 absent; 409 phase/staleness/idempotency; 422 scenario/schema; 503 unavailable runner
request_rules.mutation_id: Every POST body requires request_id, a caller-generated UUID. Same actor + endpoint + request_id + same body returns original result; changed body returns 409. Persist this across restarts.

runner_rules: Trusted driver, public/held-out tests and reference implementation are engine-owned; contestant code cannot replace them. Run candidate code in a disposable Docker container with no network, no credentials, no Docker socket, read-only source/test mounts, temporary writable scratch, CPU/memory/process limits and a timeout.
Candidate code has no third-party dependency installation in MVP. Fixed Python runtime image is prepared before demo; record image/driver identity in runner_digest.

Challenge scenario must pass the trusted reference, then fail the exact frozen target twice in fresh environments to be reproduced. Reference mismatch -> invalid; inconsistent target results or infrastructure failure -> inconclusive. Do not require a feature test to pass an unimplemented base.

Operator confirms that the expected behavior matches cited requirements before accepting a reproduced challenge. Reference is evidence of the frozen spec, not an infallible semantic judge. Suspected reference defects block acceptance until corrected with a versioned task/new match.
Eligibility requires fresh full verification of baseline plus held-out plus ALL accepted regressions, and resolved review. Report known coverage and limitations; do not claim bug-free code.
On restart preserve jobs/results/idempotency in SQLite; mark interrupted running jobs error and require rerun via finalize from decision. Never leave a false running or passed status.
Finalizing from decision is also allowed solely to rerun full verification after runner recovery. It does not change candidates, tests, spec or consume a repair round.

Practice job results are never copied into Candidate.verification and never establish eligibility. The same Verification-shaped payload is labelled by Job.kind=practice and its public/practice suite digest; the UI must visibly distinguish it from full official verification.

runtime_layout.agent_registered_root: <state_dir>/workers/{slot}; stable and pre-created before Switch onboarding
runtime_layout.editable_checkout: <state_dir>/workers/{slot}/worktree; separate Git clone of sanitized bundled task repo
runtime_layout.opponent_review_copy: <state_dir>/workers/{slot}/review/<candidate_id>; absent until reveal, read-only snapshot; engine stages it within the reviewer registered slot root and returns this path in Assignment.review_path so normal agent workspace access can read it
runtime_layout.ownership: A provisions directories, task Git base, tokens, snapshots and digests. B configures native Switch agents to use these paths and installs client/prompts. Agents commit their own allowed changes before check/submit. Never reset the real product repository or a teammate checkout. Reset only marked disposable task worktrees while no active match.

runtime_limits: candidate_budget_minutes is a declared/advisory build budget in this native-runtime MVP, not an enforced provider token quota. Record observed timing and disclose interruptions. Engine timeouts/cancellation govern its own runner jobs. They do not promise to kill a native Switch agent turn; stop that turn in its host/Console if needed. After match cancellation further mutations are refused.

scenario_semantics.bounds: Validate operation, argument count/types as JSON data and limits before execution. Permit invalid business input such as zero/negative/noninteger seats to test BOOK-06; do not confuse business-invalid values with malformed scenario structure. Candidate exceptions are failures; runner/transport errors are inconclusive.
scenario_semantics.equality: Type-strict structural JSON equality: boolean true is not integer 1; object key ordering irrelevant; array ordering relevant. Null/floats not valid expected values for this task. Preserve bool/int types in hashes.
scenario_semantics.state_assertions: To prove no mutation, include available/reservations steps after the failed booking/cancellation; a return-value assertion alone does not prove state invariants. UI examples include these checks.

transport.digests: lowercase SHA-256 hex; computed by engine

Assignment.task_spec: object equal to booking_contract for booking-v1

Scenario.steps: Step[]; 1..30 entries; fresh BookingSystem per scenario

Step.args: JSON array in callable positional order

visibility_rules.after_reveal: Both slots see frozen candidates, shared challenges, reproduction results and public evidence. Assignment supplies only the requesting slot workspace and its read-only opponent review copy. Review/repair intentionally share accepted challenge details.
visibility_rules.always: Apply the same authorization/projection to match, events, jobs and artifacts. Never include other-slot writable paths, tokens, hidden fixtures or reference source in responses. Held-out failures may show check IDs and concise failure summaries, not test source. One local OS account is still a cooperative demo, not a hostile-agent confidentiality boundary.
visibility_rules.before_reveal: Operator sees all. Slot sees its own Assignment/workspace, candidate, practice/verification jobs, logs and events plus common task/phase metadata. Opponent candidate is null; opponent jobs/challenges/events/artifact IDs absent. Opponent review_path and target_candidate_id null. Hidden test content/reference source never exposed by API.
